text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Belgian bank insurer Fortis and Dutch financial services group ING have both had to cede ground to two other concerns in Belgium as mergers sweep the industry there. (p1)
- Entertainment group Endemol sells its minority stake in Sport7 TV channel to its major shareholders Joop van den Ende and John de Mol. (p1)
- Dutch unemployment figures in September stabilise at level of the previous two months. (p1)
- Industrial concern Stork doubts a restart of aircraft maker Fokker under Korea's Samsung's charge. (p1)
- Civil engineering consultancy Heidemij buys remaining 30 pct of shares to fully own subsidiary Grabowsky & Poort. (p3)
- Bedroom furniture retailer Beter Bed, which debuts on the bourse at the end of the year, takes over rival Dormael. (p3)
- 158 businesses take utility company PNEM to court over power failure. (p3)
- Philips Electronics' new Dfl 1.7 bn chips plant will not be located in the Netherlands. (p4)
VOLKSKRANT
- Cabinet demands changes in France's European drugs policy proposal. (p1)
- Cabinet and parliament clash on night flights to and from Beek Airport in Zuid-Limburg province. (p1)
- Henny te Beest, head of Amsterdam Stock Exchange's compliance and enforcement dept, resigns, effective Jan 1. (p2)
- Rabobank staff gets advice on clothing. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Founder of bankrupt Albeco diamond investment fund, arrested for alleged fraud and culpable bankruptcy. (p3)
- Software company Baank takes over U.S. firm Antalys. (p25)
- Dutch businesses invest in computers and software again after years of stagnation. (p25)
- Packaging concern Thomassen & Drijver-Verblifa to be split up. (p26)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- 1.8 million people in the Netherlands live in an intolerable neighbourhood, according to nationwide research. (p1)
- Dutch road transporters hit by long delay at border between Poland and Belarus. (p12)
TROUW
- Cabinet takes measures to counteract the millennium problem for its computers. (p4)
- Kitchen producer Hans Verkerk to expand in Germany. (p12)
